methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Virginia Tech researchers look to AI to ease difficult workplace conversations
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech developing specialized AI training tools signals deep capability development, but originating from a research institution rather than distributed peer networks suggests concentration in academic hubs rather than broad workplace adoption.

signals.title: RiverStreet Networks removed from multiple broadband deployment projects in rural Virginia after years of delays
signals.signal_reading: Infrastructure failure affecting 30,000+ rural customers in Southwest Virginia directly undermines the foundational connectivity required for any AI adoption scenario, reinforcing the conditions that prevent both depth and distribution.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab focused on preparing leaders for AI integration suggests institutional investment in building local capacity for deep understanding rather than passive platform consumption, potentially seeding peer-to-peer knowledge transfer beyond metro concentrations.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: The VCU-AI Ready RVA partnership explicitly targets community-wide AI education and innovation, representing intentional infrastructure for distributed capability-building that could democratize deep AI fluency beyond traditional tech sector boundaries.

signals.title: From AI cameras to drones, Fairfax Co. uses new technology in policing
signals.signal_reading: Fairfax County deploying advanced AI cameras and drones for policing demonstrates deep technical implementation capacity concentrated in wealthy NoVA jurisdictions with resources smaller Virginia localities cannot replicate, widening the capability gap.
